newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria telecom company increases transit traffic.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria telecom company increases transit traffic.

text.p: Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC) plans a big increase in the volume of telecom traffic this year with the completion of a digital overlay network (DON) on its territory, officials said on Tuesday.
"We expect to receive this year $15-$20 million from transit traffic," BTC chairman Mihail Danov told a news conference.
BTC, which aims to modernise the country's antiquated telephone links to European standards, plans to complete a DON on its territory by July 1997.
Danov said Telia AB of Sweden had agreed to bring transit traffic to BTC and the signed protocol was the first of this kind in Bulgaria's telecommunications history.
He said Telia was a general traffic carrier for a number of countries, including the Baltic countries, Norway and Finland.
Negotiations for bringing transit traffic to BTC were now under way with Global One, the joint venture of Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom and Sprint Corp, Danov said.
"We hope to sign an agreement with Global One for a quite big volume of traffic via Bulgaria," he added.
BTC plans to start negotiations also with AT&T Corp of the United States, which is BTC's biggest carrier to the Americas and the Far East, Danov said.
"We will offer to permit them to move part of their traffic via Bulgaria," Danov said, adding that negotiations on this point were expected to start within the next two weeks.
AT&T has submitted its offers for ensuring Internet services in the country, he said.
Bulgaria and Turkey plan to open officially an optic cable link on February 12 and another link between Bulgaria and Romania will be opened by the end of February, officials said.
A digital cable linked Bulgaria with its western Balkan neighbours Yugoslavia and Macedonia last year.

BTC has been granted loans worth $150 million for the DON programme from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, the European Investment Bank and the World Bank for part of the project. BTC is providing the rest of the funds.
The company will start its payments to the banks this year and its 1996 financial results showed revenues of some 35 billion levs, Danov said. He did not say what the profit was.
"This summer we will discuss with the three banks extending new credits for the development of Bulgarian telecommunications," Danov said.

Bulgaria plans to call a tender for the sale of a 25 percent stake in BTC this year and seeks a strategic partner among the world's telecom leaders. The cabinet has shortlisted six banks which bid to advise the government in the sale and their offers should be received by February 10.
